memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: follow‑up of migraine and iron‑deficiency anaemia.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports occasional throbbing frontal headaches, relieved by sumatriptan, and mild fatigue. No new neurologic symptoms.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 71 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 24.6 (overweight). Pulse regular, cardiopulmonary exam normal. Neurologic exam: no focal deficits, mild tenderness over temples.
IMPRESSION: 1. Migraine, prophylactic propranolol continued. 2. Iron‑deficiency anaemia, Hb 10.2 g/dL, ferritin 12 ng/mL, MCV 78 fL – to start oral iron. Ordered fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar as annual screen.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, continue propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, naproxen 500 mg SOS, topiramate 25 mg HS. Advise iron‑rich diet, avoid tea with meals, walk 30 min daily. Return if headache worsens, vomiting, black stools, fever >39°C, or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: review of anaemia and migraine control.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Headaches reduced to 1‑2 per week, sumatriptan used twice. Fatigue better, but reports mild constipation from iron.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82, weight 70.5 kg, BMI 24.4 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly.
IMPRESSION: Migraine well controlled on prophylactic propranolol. Iron‑deficiency anaemia improving; Hb rising, constipation likely iron‑related. Continue iron, consider alternate‑day dosing to reduce GI side effects. Annual lipid/FBS pending.
ARRANGEMENTS: Change ferrous sulfate to 200 mg on alternate days. Continue other meds. Advise increase fibre, water, and take iron with orange juice. Return if headache frequency >3/week, severe constipation, melena, or BP >150/95.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: autumn review, influenza vaccine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Headaches occasional, well‑controlled. No fatigue. Reports good tolerance of iron.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80, weight 70 kg, BMI 24.2 (overweight). Lungs clear, heart regular S1S2.
IMPRESSION: Migraine stable on propranolol. Iron‑deficiency anaemia: Hb 11.6 g/dL, ferritin 22 ng/mL, MCV 80 fL – improving. Ordered fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar (annual). Influenza vaccine indicated given age >60.
ARRANGEMENTS: Give inactivated influenza vaccine today (05‑Oct‑2025). Continue ferrous sulfate alternate days, propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan SOS, naproxen SOS, topiramate HS. Advise maintain activity, diet rich in leafy greens. Return if new neurologic symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or bleeding.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: worsening migraine frequency.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports three migraine episodes in past week, each lasting 6‑8 hours, associated nausea, relieved by sumatriptan. Fatigue mild.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/86, weight 71.2 kg, BMI 24.6 (overweight). Neurologic exam: no new deficits, mild scalp tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Migraine breakthrough – consider adding topiramate dose increase or short‑term NSAID review. Iron‑deficiency anaemia stable: Hb 12.0 g/dL, ferritin 28 ng/mL, MCV 82 fL.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase topiramate to 50 mg HS. Continue ferrous sulfate alternate days, propranolol 40 mg OD, sumatriptan SOS, naproxen SOS. Advise headache diary, regular sleep, hydration. Return if headache >5/week, visual loss, weakness, speech difficulty, or BP >160/100.
